title: The Fall Guy (2024) shows how far the action comedy has fallen since ... The Interview (2014)

commenti.body: So like comedy is supposed to make me laugh, i laughed way more in the fall guy and the action is better in my opinion you talk about stunts but did not mention the car roll broke a world record for the 8 and a half cannon roll, i loved the banter between the stunt coordinator and gosling, quoting rocky, fast and furious and lord of the rings is creating the dynamic between them and i found it fun to try and guess along, also relationships and messy emotional its not always so simple as the  aggrieved party should understand and irrational hate is normal when someone ghosts you, im really not trying to dive to deep here but with all that said if the interview was more funny for you thats really all that matters in a comedy. The movie star and producer are not developed intentionally as they play a stereotypical role in the film anyway. The action when hes high in the club looked amazing in my opinion as well and the boat scene. Howard Hughes once said a good film is three good scenes and no bad ones and the fall guy fits that billing for me more so than the interview.

I thoroughly enjoyed The Fall guy and I remember thoroughly enjoying the Interview back when it came out.  


Mind you, I saw Fall Guy in the cinema, and therefor didn't see any of the stuff that's in the extended cut. I imagine a lot of it was cut for a reason, namely to streamline the narrative. 

In any case, I find Fall Guy to be an old school action-comedy type of thing, like the 00s Charlie's Angels or Jackie Chan movies were. Comparing that to The Interview, which is more about wacky situational comedy seems misguided to me.

But of course, it's always down to preference in the end.
